The run ended with a LoopBreakStop exception after 63 episodes, with reward 0.0 [R0M.trace_lab]. That exception is not a budget ceiling, an infra failure or a completion, so the stop reason is other. The harness had already warned "you are repeating; change approach or finish" [T0B116:<RANGE>you are repeating; change approach or finish</RANGE>].

The model wrote both the pandas and SQL implementations in place. The pandas rename built its mapping backwards, keyed by the new name: "to_rename = {new_name: simple_varname(old_name) for new_name, old_name in kwargs.items()}" [T0B60:<RANGE>to_rename = {new_name: simple_varname(old_name) for new_name, old_name in kwargs.items()}</RANGE>]. That edit is wrong because pandas' `rename(columns=...)` expects old names as keys. The model's own test then showed the columns unchanged: "['a', 'b', 'c']" [T0B74:<RANGE>['a', 'b', 'c']</RANGE>].

The model also found that `simple_varname(_.a)` returns "simple_varname(_.a): None" [T0B80:<RANGE>simple_varname(_.a): None</RANGE>]. The verb wrapper likely strips symbols, but the model never checked or adapted. Instead it repeated the same sed command many times, starting at "sed -n 2110,2140p" [T0B109:<RANGE>sed -n 2110,2140p /workspace/repo/siuba/dply/verbs.py; echo ====; sed -n 840,900p /workspace/repo/siuba/dply/verbs.py</RANGE>]. It kept going through to the last turn [T0B125:<RANGE>sed -n 2110,2140p /workspace/repo/siuba/dply/verbs.py; echo ====; sed -n 840,900p /workspace/repo/siuba/dply/verbs.py</RANGE>]. That is 9 identical calls (B109–B125), slightly below the threshold of 10. Counting the preceding near-duplicate debugging turns that also made no progress, the stalled stretch exceeds 10 turns. The harness break was explicitly repetition-driven, so I label the loop repetition.

There was no upstream fetch.
